GitHub Issue:
Post Date: 2016-05-08T11:36:00Z
Current Date: April 4 2025
Title: Throwing an error in callback results in "Unhandled rejection Error: Callback was already called."
Description: Throwing an error in callback results in "Unhandled rejection Error: Callback was already called."
This prevents user from seeing actual error message, created by assertions in tests. 
This hasn't been happening in 2.0.0-rc3. Is this expected behaviour in rc4?

Here's the example code

``` js
async.waterfall([
  (next) => {
    apiClient
      .post('/some-url')
      .send({prop: 'value'})
      .expect(200)
      .end(next);
  }
], (err) => {
  assert.ifError(err);
  throw new Error('Some Error');
});
```

The problem can be analyzed and verified without needing to build or run the code in a dedicated environment. The issue describes a specific behavior change between versions 2.0.0-rc3 and rc4 where throwing an error in a callback results in an "Unhandled rejection Error: Callback was already called" message instead of showing the actual error.

This is a conceptual issue related to how the async library handles errors and callbacks. An LLM can analyze the code snippet provided and understand the expected behavior versus the actual behavior. The solution would likely involve understanding the proper way to handle errors in async callbacks or identifying if this is indeed a regression in the library.
